In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the binding between GAGs and PLs is not a simple process, and it depends on the nature of the GAGs and the PLs.
both GAGs bind lipids at similar rates, except for 16:0-PE, which binds to CS at a much higher level.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have shown the importance of the interaction between glycosaminoglysans and phospholipid in synovial fluid, which may be important to understand the lubrication process of the synovium.
the interaction of hyaluronic acid and chondroitine with phospholipid molecules in synovial fluid is governed by the hydrogen bonds.

the interaction between glycosaminogylcan and lipid molecules is mainly hydrogen bonding, and that the hydrogen bonding between glycosaminogylycan and lipids is stronger when the glycosaminogycan molecule is in a folded conformation.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the molecular interactions between the two main synovial fluid components, glycosamino glycan and phospholipid, may play a key role in the tribological properties of synovial fluid.
GAGs can bind lipids at the nanoscale level and that the type of lipids and their interaction with GAGs may have a significant effect on the tribological properties of synovial fluid.
the interaction of the synovium fluid components is not random but rather selective.
